reason: The history row dated June 30, 2026 states EC2 Global View is now renamed AWS Global View and shows EC2 and other supported resources across all Regions in a single view.
The instance types history rows give R8g (memory optimized, Graviton4) on July 9, 2024 and M8g (general purpose) and C8g (compute optimized) on September 25, 2024.
The history rows give M9g and M9gd (general purpose, Graviton5) on June 9, 2026 and R9g and R9gd (memory optimized, Graviton5) on August 31, 2026.

Two history rows dated July 30, 2024 state hibernation for newly launched instances on the eleven listed types and for instances launched from an Amazon Linux or Ubuntu AMI that supports Graviton instance types.
The history row dated March 25, 2024 states you can set all new EC2 instance launches in your account to use IMDSv2 by default.
The history row dated February 24, 2026 states IMDSv2 can be enforced at the account level for each Region and that, when enforced, instances only launch if configured to require IMDSv2.
The EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint row dated June 13, 2023 states connection through SSH or RDP without the instance needing a public IPv4 address.
The row dated November 21, 2025 states Interruptible Capacity Reservations make unused capacity temporarily available for other workloads within your account.
The row dated December 1, 2024 states you can now view Amazon EC2 managed instances in the EC2 console.
The row dated February 16, 2026 states you can run hypervisors such as Hyper-V and KVM inside virtualized EC2 instances; non-bare metal is a gloss of virtualized.
The row dated June 29, 2026 states a precision-time placement group places instances on hardware with direct access to high-precision time sources.

The row dated November 10, 2022 states an EC2 Fleet using price-capacity-optimized looks at price and capacity to pick the pools least likely to be interrupted with the lowest possible price; the adjacent row covers Spot Fleet.

The quotes support the current charge on all public IPv4 addresses and no charge before February 1, 2024 for the in-use row, but the claim drops that row's scope and the next table row shows an additional (secondary) Elastic IP on a running instance was already charged $0.005 per hour, so 'an in-use public IPv4 address had no charge' is too broad.
The row dated October 24, 2023 states Spot Instances can be hibernated with the same hibernation experience and instance families available for On-Demand Instances.

The history row dates T8i to September 15, 2026, and the What's New page calls them burstable, with up to 30% better price performance than T3, four sizes nano to medium, and the T3 CPU credit system with Standard and Unlimited modes.
The decision guide states that with multiple active commitment types AWS applies Reserved Instances first, then EC2 Instance Savings Plans, then Compute Savings Plans.
The quote states Elastic Beanstalk is specifically designed for web applications and provides the runtime on EC2 instances so you deploy only your code.

The quote, read with the sentence just before it in context (managing EC2 involves setup, scaling, patching and securing), states this can require a dedicated operations team and is often justified where granular control is necessary.
The quote states Fargate is a technology used with Amazon ECS to run containers without managing servers or clusters of EC2 instances.
The compute decision guide states horizontal scalability is essential for dynamic workloads with fluctuating demands.
The quote states serverless options like Lambda run code in response to events without managing servers, reducing operational burden.
The quote defines vertical as scaling up by adding power such as CPU or memory, and horizontal as scaling out by adding instances.
The quotes state Compute Optimizer gives EC2 recommendations to improve performance, save money, or both, and analyzes existing instance specifications and utilization metrics.
Under the None classification (no recommendations), the quote gives opted in less than 12 hours, running less than 30 hours, or an unsupported instance type, with 'might'.
The Requirements section states you must first opt in to Compute Optimizer to get recommendations.
The quote gives the over-provisioned definition word for word, including the no-under-provisioned condition and the unnecessary cost.
The quote gives the under-provisioned definition and that it might lead to poor application performance.
The quote states Compute Savings Plans apply across all Regions so the discount follows the workload, including failover, and EC2 Instance Savings Plans are scoped to a specific Region.
The quotes state on-demand scalable capacity, launching as many or as few virtual servers as needed, adding capacity for compute-heavy tasks or traffic spikes, and scaling down when usage decreases.
The console steps state that with Reboot instance cleared EC2 does not shut down and reboot the instance and AWS can't guarantee file system integrity of the image.
The quote states EC2 powers down the instance before creating the AMI for a consistent state, and you can tell it not to power down and reboot if you are confident of consistency.

The quotes state snapshots of the root and all attached EBS volumes are created and charged until the AMI is deregistered and snapshots deleted, and that instance store volumes of new instances contain no data from the source instance.
The quote states predictable but variable workloads benefit from Savings Plans for the baseline and On-Demand Capacity Reservations or Capacity Blocks for predictable peaks.
The blog states there is a charge for data transfer across Regions that depends on the source and destination Region.
The blog states there is no charge for inbound data transfer across all services in all Regions and outbound to the internet is charged per service at originating-Region rates.
The blog states data transfer within the same Availability Zone is free and that charges apply for cross-Availability Zone communication between the EC2 instances.

Under Host affinity (configured at the instance level per context), the quotes state Host means always restarting on the same host, and Default means any available host with a best-effort try of the last host.

Under Auto-placement (configured at the host level per context), the quotes state disabled accepts only launches naming the host ID and is the default for new hosts, and enabled accepts untargeted host-tenancy launches matching the instance type configuration.
Under On-Demand Dedicated Hosts, the quote states the price varies by family and Region and you pay per second with a 60-second minimum for the active host regardless of instance quantity or size.
The quote states that, subject to Microsoft licensing terms, you can bring Windows Server and SQL Server licenses to Dedicated Hosts with no additional software charge.
